projects.why: A local reference for how a product UI project should be captured as a suite: dashboard, detail, settings, flows, states, and reusable components are recorded together instead of flattening the product into one representative screen.
A high-signal reference for AI-era product operations: triage, issue ownership, project planning, cycles, and analytics all read as one compact operating system instead of separate admin tools.
projects.framework: Linear web app and docs capture

projects.why: A strong reference for turning a keyboard launcher into a multi-surface productivity system: store discovery, AI chat, notes, focus, and team workflows all stay lightweight and command-first.
projects.framework: Raycast product site and feature pages

projects.why: A high-signal reference for AI-first email triage: view-building, auto-labeling, block-style drafting, and meeting scheduling turn a personal inbox into a configurable workflow console. Notion has announced the product will shut down on 2026-09-22, so this is a time-bounded but still useful UI reference.
projects.framework: Notion Mail product and help center capture

projects.why: A strong reference for premium email-as-workspace design: split inboxes, AI drafting, reusable snippets, follow-up cues, and team collaboration all stay fast and keyboard-native instead of turning into a bloated suite shell.
projects.framework: Superhuman product site and help center capture

surfaces.title: Operations dashboard
surfaces.study: Dense metrics, activity, and task queues share one scan rhythm without turning into a decorative landing page.
surfaces.reuse: Use for operational products that need a calm command center.

surfaces.title: Task detail
surfaces.study: Primary object detail keeps status, timeline, owners, and actions visible around one work item.
surfaces.reuse: Use when records need context and action in the same view.

surfaces.title: Team settings
surfaces.study: Settings preserve product density through compact rows, grouped permissions, and direct integration controls.
surfaces.reuse: Use for team administration surfaces that should not become long form dumps.

surfaces.title: Triage queue
surfaces.study: Cross-team intake, customer support handoff, and issue routing are treated as one dense queue rather than a thin notification feed.
surfaces.reuse: Use for work queues that need fast scanning, ownership, and escalation in the same surface.

surfaces.title: Project workspace
surfaces.study: Projects keep overview, milestones, docs, and linked issue views close to one execution unit without losing planning context.
surfaces.reuse: Use when feature-sized work needs a durable home between roadmap and issue detail.

surfaces.title: Cycle planning controls
surfaces.study: Cadence, calendars, capacity, and automations are configured as lightweight controls around a recurring planning rhythm.
surfaces.reuse: Use for recurring planning systems that need guardrails without turning into heavyweight configuration.

surfaces.title: Insights analytics
surfaces.study: Real-time issue analytics and custom insights give teams a native analysis surface instead of exporting planning data elsewhere.
surfaces.reuse: Use when operational products need trend visibility inside the primary workspace.

surfaces.title: Extension store
surfaces.study: Search, browse, and install flows are presented as a lightweight catalog that still feels native to a launcher product.
surfaces.reuse: Use for plugin ecosystems that need discovery without forcing a heavy marketplace shell.

surfaces.title: AI chat workspace
surfaces.study: Raycast AI frames chat, commands, and model selection as one assistant surface tied directly to OS-level actions.
surfaces.reuse: Use when conversational AI should feel like an extension of the working environment, not a detached chatbot tab.

surfaces.title: Notes capture surface
surfaces.study: Meeting notes, todos, and markdown editing are kept frictionless enough to justify capture from anywhere in the system.
surfaces.reuse: Use for quick-entry writing surfaces that must stay faster than opening a full editor.

surfaces.title: Team workspace configuration
surfaces.study: Shared snippets, quicklinks, and extension templates turn team operations into a managed layer without losing the product's individual speed.
surfaces.reuse: Use for products that expand from personal utility into team-scale workflow standardization.

surfaces.title: Focus session controls
surfaces.study: Distraction blocking is packaged as a lightweight mode rather than a separate wellness product, keeping the intervention close to everyday work.
surfaces.reuse: Use for optional focus states that should feel integrated, not bolted on.

surfaces.title: AI-labeled views inbox
surfaces.study: Priority, custom views, and AI labels make the default inbox read like an operator queue instead of one undifferentiated message feed.
surfaces.reuse: Use for message-heavy products that need users to move between personal priorities, saved views, and automation-generated organization.

surfaces.title: Thread navigation and full-page message context
surfaces.study: Thread list, reading pane, and full-page message modes keep skim and deep work in the same product grammar.
surfaces.reuse: Use when a communication tool should support quick triage and extended message work without a separate detail app.

surfaces.title: Composer with snippets, AI drafting, and scheduled send
surfaces.study: Drafting combines reusable snippets, AI writing help, and send scheduling so composition feels like workflow setup, not just message entry.
surfaces.reuse: Use for compose surfaces that should blend authoring, reuse, and timing controls in one panel.

surfaces.title: Inbox rules, notifications, and view configuration
surfaces.study: Notification scope, inbox behavior, and account preferences are grouped around working habits rather than buried in generic mail settings.
surfaces.reuse: Use for products where settings should reinforce the core workflow model instead of feeling like a detached admin surface.

surfaces.title: Mobile inbox triage companion
surfaces.study: Mobile keeps fast triage, search, and reply loops available without trying to reproduce every dense desktop control at full depth.
surfaces.reuse: Use for companion mobile surfaces that need to preserve the product's organization model while cutting down interaction density.

surfaces.title: Custom split inbox
surfaces.study: Work is divided into role-specific lanes so dense message volume becomes a set of operating queues rather than one overwhelming chronological list.
surfaces.reuse: Use for communication products that need multiple first-class working modes inside the same feed.

surfaces.title: Ask AI and thread-level assistance
surfaces.study: AI help is embedded alongside the message thread, so summarizing, researching, and drafting feel like accelerators on top of normal email work.
surfaces.reuse: Use when AI support should feel like an in-context copilot rather than a detached assistant page.

surfaces.title: Compose with snippets and AI writing
surfaces.study: Reusable snippets and AI drafting keep composition optimized for speed while still letting users personalize high-frequency outbound messages.
surfaces.reuse: Use for products where repetitive writing should become a configurable system instead of a manual task.

surfaces.title: Shared conversations and team coordination
surfaces.study: Team visibility and collaboration features extend the inbox into a lightweight operations surface without requiring a separate admin console.
surfaces.reuse: Use for products that need collaboration to emerge from the primary workspace rather than from an external back office.

surfaces.title: Mobile follow-up and triage
surfaces.study: Mobile focuses on quick triage, reply, and follow-up loops while keeping the product's premium speed and keyboard-mindset intact where possible.
surfaces.reuse: Use for mobile companion surfaces that should preserve pace and hierarchy without copying every desktop affordance.

flows.title: Queue to detail to resolution
flows.study: The core flow moves from dashboard scanning to detail review to a final action without losing global context.
flows.reuse: Use for approval, triage, and operations workflows.

flows.title: Triage to delegated issue ownership
flows.study: New work moves from a shared queue into delegated ownership without breaking the product's compact navigation model.
flows.reuse: Use for intake-heavy products that need a clear handoff from queue review to accountable execution.

flows.title: Project planning into cycle rhythm
flows.study: Project scope, cycle settings, and analytics form one closed loop between planning, execution, and follow-up measurement.
flows.reuse: Use for products that want planning configuration to feel connected to day-to-day delivery.

flows.title: Command to capture or AI output
flows.study: The launcher routes users quickly into note capture or AI completion without switching mental models.
flows.reuse: Use for keyboard-first products that need zero-friction branching into different work modes.

flows.title: Personal utility into team workflow
flows.study: Teams adds shared building blocks on top of the personal launcher instead of replacing it with a separate enterprise console.
flows.reuse: Use when a solo tool expands into organizational workflow without losing product taste.

flows.title: Prompt-driven setup into persistent custom views
flows.study: Users can describe how they want mail organized, then refine that setup into stable custom views and AI labeling rules.
flows.reuse: Use when onboarding should translate a fuzzy workflow request into a durable working layout.

flows.title: Compose to schedule to calendar coordination
flows.study: Writing, scheduling, and meeting booking live in one loop, so outbound mail feels connected to time management rather than a separate app handoff.
flows.reuse: Use when an email or messaging product needs to connect composition directly to scheduling intent.

flows.title: Split inbox to follow-up loop
flows.study: Messages move from category-specific inbox lanes into reminders and follow-up actions without losing the user's chosen working structure.
flows.reuse: Use for products where review is really a repeated triage-and-return rhythm.

flows.title: Personal inbox into shared team handling
flows.study: Shared conversations let an individual inbox become a team surface without collapsing everything into a generic collaborative dashboard.
flows.reuse: Use when a single-player tool needs to expand into team work while preserving personal speed.

states.title: Empty queue
states.study: The empty state explains what changed and keeps one useful next action visible.
states.reuse: Use for first-run or completed workflow states.

states.title: High-density table
states.study: Rows preserve object, owner, status, and risk without oversized card treatment.
states.reuse: Use when repeated action matters more than marketing-style display.

states.title: High-density planning surfaces
states.study: Queues, project lists, and analytics views preserve dense metadata without collapsing into noisy card galleries.
states.reuse: Use when a product's value depends on compact scan rhythm and repeated table-like interaction.

states.title: Search-heavy discovery and command states
states.study: Store results, AI commands, and quick-entry tools stay legible under dense keyboard-driven interaction.
states.reuse: Use when a product's default state is fast search, not long-form browsing.

states.title: Multi-view inbox density
states.study: The product stays legible while showing parallel categories, labels, and threaded conversations in a compact split-pane layout.
states.reuse: Use when communication products need more than one simultaneous organizing dimension.

states.title: High-volume triage state
states.study: Split inboxes, shortcuts, and AI assistance keep large message volume workable without forcing the user into a heavy tabbed console.
states.reuse: Use when information density should be tamed by structure and acceleration, not by reducing throughput.

components.title: Persistent product rail
components.study: A stable left rail keeps surfaces discoverable while the working area changes.
components.reuse: Use for multi-surface consoles with repeated navigation.

components.title: Activity and review stack
components.study: Compact stacked panels keep flow status and exceptions visible next to the primary work surface.
components.reuse: Use for collaborative dashboards and review queues.

components.title: Persistent team-and-object sidebar
components.study: Teams, issues, projects, cycles, and insights stay one click away through a stable navigation spine.
components.reuse: Use for multi-surface work tools that should feel like one operating environment.

components.title: Saved views and queue filters
components.study: Filtering is embedded into everyday workflow rather than hidden in an advanced search screen.
components.reuse: Use when every team needs to shape the same data model into different operational views.

components.title: Compact issue and project lists
components.study: List rows carry status, ownership, timing, and project context without oversized chrome.
components.reuse: Use for products where editing and scanning happen from the same dense list surface.

components.title: Launcher as primary control surface
components.study: One command surface anchors discovery, invocation, and automation across otherwise different product areas.
components.reuse: Use when many capabilities should feel reachable through one consistent interaction grammar.

components.title: Store search and browse controls
components.study: The ecosystem layer uses simple search-first filtering instead of dense faceted chrome.
components.reuse: Use for add-on galleries that should preserve speed and clarity.

components.title: Lightweight product family rail
components.study: Store, AI, Teams, and core features read as adjacent tools inside one product family rather than separate brands.
components.reuse: Use for software suites that need breadth without enterprise navigation bloat.

components.title: View-first sidebar
components.study: Saved views and account navigation sit at the product spine, making organization the primary control model.
components.reuse: Use for products where navigation should be built around working lenses instead of fixed feature tabs.

components.title: Labels, grouping, and search controls
components.study: Filters and AI-applied labels shape one inbox into several focused operating modes without duplicating data.
components.reuse: Use when one communication stream needs multiple role-specific reading modes.

components.title: Keyboard-first inbox actions
components.study: Fast actions for triage, reply, scheduling, and navigation keep the product feeling closer to a workspace than a traditional mailbox.
components.reuse: Use when speed and repeatability matter enough to justify a keyboard interaction layer.

components.title: Keyboard-first action model
components.study: The product's primary grammar is fast command execution, which keeps advanced actions feeling lightweight.
components.reuse: Use when repeated communication work benefits from one consistent command layer.

components.title: Split inbox rules and lane controls
components.study: Inbox rules act like persistent filters that shape attention before the user reads individual threads.
components.reuse: Use for products where organization should happen upstream of item review.

components.title: Minimal rail around message work
components.study: Navigation stays intentionally spare so the product feels premium and fast even as more AI and team features accumulate.
components.reuse: Use when breadth should not force a product into enterprise-console chrome.
